swap_rate_curve.text: `ois_curve_sonia_sofr` and `swap_rate_curve` run in opposite directions. `ois_curve_sonia_sofr` starts from quoted OIS swap rates (`ois_rates`) at given `maturities` and bootstraps a discount curve from them, so it answers "what discount factors and zero rates do these market quotes imply?" `swap_rate_curve` starts from a set of discount factors (`discount_factors`) and returns the par swap rate for each tenor, so it answers "what fixed rate makes a par swap worth zero on this curve?" Both take `maturities` and a fixed-leg `frequency`, which defaults to 1 per year. In practice, you could use the first to build a curve from quotes and the second to check which par rates a given curve implies.

explain.text: `ois_curve_sonia_sofr` (OIS Curve SONIA SOFR) builds a discount curve from quoted OIS swap rates for SONIA or SOFR. You pass in `ois_rates` (decimal rate per maturity) and `maturities` (in years, ascending), plus an optional `frequency` for fixed-leg payments per year, which defaults to 1. It bootstraps the curve the same way as for par swaps, using single-curve OIS discounting: each discount factor comes from the quoted rate and the running sum of earlier discounted accruals. The discount factors are also expressed as zero rates, so you get a curve you can use to discount cash flows.

when.text:
`ois_curve_sonia_sofr` (OIS Curve SONIA SOFR) fits when you need a discount curve built from quoted overnight-indexed swap rates.

- You have OIS quotes (SONIA or SOFR) at a set of maturities and want discount factors and zero rates from them.
- You want single-curve OIS discounting, where the curve is bootstrapped the same way as for par swaps.
- Your fixed leg pays at a regular frequency. The default is annual, and you can change it with `frequency`.
- Your quotes are decimals with maturities in years, ascending.

If your inputs are different, a related function may suit you better:
- `bootstrap_yield_curve`: bootstraps zero (spot) rates from par-coupon bond rates.
